dish: Handmade yellowtail fishball and pork-ball noodles, dry or soup
address: Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, #02-28/29, 44 Holland Drive, Singapore 270044
w: A MICHELIN Bib Gourmand hawker across two adjoining stalls: noodle soup or 'dry' noodles with minced pork, pork balls or fish balls hand-made on the spot — the yellowtail fishballs are the draw.

dish: Handmade fishball noodles and mushroom minced-meat noodles (bak chor mee)
address: Holland Village Market & Food Centre, #01-14, 1 Lorong Mambong, Singapore 277700
w: A fishball-noodle lineage going back to a 1946 Chinatown pushcart: hand-made fishballs over springy mee pok ($4/$5) or a mushroom bak chor mee — the heritage bowl of Holland Village's food centre.

dish: Katong laksa (fragrant, coconut-dried-shrimp gravy) and nasi lemak
address: Holland Village Market & Food Centre, #01-15, 1 Lorong Mambong, Singapore 277700
w: A laksa that leans fragrant rather than fiery — prawns, fishcake, cockles and tau pok in a dried-shrimp-and-coconut gravy (premium $6.80) — beside a nasi lemak spread refined over decades.

dish: Economical fried bee hoon with sambal chicken wing, egg and vegetables
address: Holland Village Market & Food Centre, #01-11, 1 Lorong Mambong, Singapore 277700
w: The neighbourhood's breakfast stall: fried bee hoon or noodles from $1.20, topped with sambal chicken wing, egg and vegetables — sells out and shuts by early afternoon.

dish: Fried Hokkien prawn mee — white and yellow noodles in prawn-head, squid and pork-bone stock
n: Yuan Hokkien Fried Prawn Mee (Ghim Moh)
address: Ghim Moh Market & Food Centre, 20 Ghim Moh Road, Singapore 270020 (unit to confirm)
w: A Margaret Drive Food Centre transplant: white and yellow noodles wok-fried down in a rich stock of prawn heads, squid and pork bones — one of the Ghim Moh picks shared by Women's Weekly and Her World.

dish: Thai stewed beef noodle soup with beef balls, slices and tendon
n: Yuan Authentic Thai Stewed Beef Noodle (Ghim Moh)
address: Ghim Moh Market & Food Centre, 20 Ghim Moh Road, Singapore 270020 (unit to confirm)
w: Run by a cook from Chiang Rai: Thai stewed and sliced beef noodle soup — beefy, aromatic broth, beef balls, slices and tendon, small bowls from under $3 — a Thai hawker kitchen in an otherwise Chinese-heavy centre (Eatbook review; Women's Weekly and Her World Ghim Moh lists).

dish: Kway chap — flat rice sheets in herbal soy broth with braised offal, pork and egg
address: Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, #02-02, 44 Holland Drive, Singapore 270044
w: The kway chap stall Miss Tam Chiak calls chef Daniel Tay's favourite: silky rice sheets in a herbal braising broth with a spread of braised pork, offal and egg — written up by Daniel Food Diary, SG Food on Foot and in Eatbook's 13 best Holland Drive stalls.

dish: Nasi ayam penyet — smashed fried chicken with tempeh, tau kwa and sambal
address: Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, 44 Holland Drive, Singapore 270044 (unit to confirm)
w: Holland Drive's Malay stall for ayam penyet: fragrant rice, fried chicken, tempeh, tau kwa, cucumber and sambal from about $4.50-$5 — on both Eatbook's and Women's Weekly's Holland Drive lists.

dish: Char siew and roast pork (sio bak) rice
address: Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, #02-36, 44 Holland Drive, Singapore 270044
w: The $3 char siew and roast pork rice that Eatbook headlines in its Holland Drive guide; Women's Weekly also lists it among the centre's 10 best.

dish: Fried carrot cake (chai tow kway), white or black
address: Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, 44 Holland Drive, Singapore 270044 (unit to confirm)
w: Black or white chai tow kway in $3/$4/$5 portions — the carrot cake pick of both Eatbook and Women's Weekly at Holland Drive.

address: Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, #02-35, 44 Holland Drive, Singapore 270044
w: Young hawkers baking affordable shio pan from scratch inside a hawker centre — a newer Holland Drive draw named by Seth Lui's 11 best and covered by Eatbook.
